key_insight: GradAudit uses parameter gradients to identify whether a vision-language model truly learned an image-text pair during training, rather than relying on surface-level outputs.
clinical_relevance: In healthcare VLLMs, this could help audit whether sensitive medical images and reports were used in training, supporting stronger privacy and provenance checks.
method: Analyze internal gradient patterns instead of black-box outputs
Compare gradient stability/alignment for training vs non-training samples
Detect genuine cross-modal associations learned by the model
evidence_signal: Across medical and general-domain datasets, GradAudit outperformed state-of-the-art baselines in both pretraining and fine-tuning VLLMs, and it revealed underestimation of unauthorized data use in a copyrighted-content case study.
watch_item: Gradient-based auditing may require access to model internals and careful interpretation, so it may be harder to deploy for closed systems or to translate directly into legal proof of data provenance.
paper_title: Revealing Training Data Exposure in Vision Language Large Models via Parameter Gradients
